Rashi on Bava Metzia 23b:10:1.hebrew: שלא שבעתן - עדיין לא הורגל בראייתן ותשמישן שיהא מכירן יפה. ולשון אנפוריא נוטריקון: "אין פה ראיה":
Rashi on Bava Metzia 23b:10:1.english: [As the eye] has not sufficiently seen them - [The owner] has not yet become accustomed to seeing and using them such that he would recognize them well. And the term anpurya is an acronym [for] "there is no seeing here" [ein poh re'iyah].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 23b:11:1.english: The [practical] difference, etc. - And [this is] a case where this [person] who claims them is a Torah scholar.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 23b:11:2.hebrew: במסכת - "יש בידך מסכת פלוני סדורה בגירסא, או לאו?" ואע"ג שסדורה היא לו, יאמר לו: "לאו", ומדת ענוה היא:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 23b:11:2.english: With regard to a tractate - [If someone asks him,] "Do you have such-and-such a tractate fluently memorized, or not?" — even though it is fluent to him, he may say to him, "No," and it is a trait of humility.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 23b:11:3.hebrew: בפוריא - אם ישאלוהו "שימשת מטתך?" יאמר "לאו". מדת צניעות הוא:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 23b:11:3.english: With regard to a bed - [If asked,] "Did you have marital relations?" he may say, "No," [for] it is a trait of modesty.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 23b:1:1.english: With a number that is equal - The fishermen are already accustomed to stringing according to this number on a single string.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 23b:2:1.english: And fragments of lead - Broken pieces of lead.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 23b:2:2.english: That he accurately state its weights - That he state its weight and accurately state the truth.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 23b:3:1.english: With a weight that is equal - For the butchers are accustomed to make the cuts of this weight.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 23b:3:2.english: The cut itself [as] a distinguishing mark - He can say it was from such-and-such a limb.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 23b:3:3.hebrew: או דדפקא - צואר שמעתי, ומשום רבי יצחק בר' מנחם שמעתי: דדפקא — פלנק"ן, מקום שדופק כשהוא יגע:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 23b:3:3.english: Or from the dafka - I heard [that it means] the neck; and in the name of Rabbi Yitzchak b'Rabbi Menachem I heard [that] dafka [is] flanc [Old French: flank], the place that throbs when [the animal] is exerted.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 23b:3:4.hebrew: חתיכות דג חייב להכריז - קא ס"ד כשאין בהן סימן, והחתיכה גופה סימן, או מאצל הראש או מן הזנב:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 23b:3:4.english: Cuts of fish, he is obligated to proclaim - [The Gemara] initially assumes [that this is] when there is no distinguishing mark on them, and the cut itself [serves as] a distinguishing mark — either from near the head or from the tail.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 23b:3:5.english: And a bitten fish - This is its distinguishing mark.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 23b:4:1.english: With what are we dealing here - Where [the baraita] teaches [that regarding] pieces of fish, one is obligated to proclaim [them].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 23b:4:2.english: Where there is a distinguishing mark in the cut - That it was not cut in the manner of those who cut.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 23b:4:3.english: As in that [case] of Rabba - When he would send meat to his wife by the hand of a gentile.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 23b:4:4.hebrew: מחתך לה אתלת קרנתא - עושה החתיכה בת ג' קרנות כזה: (*):(*)
Rashi on Bava Metzia 23b:4:4.english: [He would] cut it with three corners - [He] makes the piece with three corners, like this: (*):(*)

Rashi on Bava Metzia 23b:4:5.english: Similar to a bitten fish - For there is a distinguishing mark on it.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 23b:5:1.english: Our Mishnah - [That is, the Mishnah] which [states that] one is obligated to proclaim [the finding].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 23b:5:2.hebrew: ברשום - חביותיהם של חרס היו, וגפין אותם במגופת חרס, ושורקין טיט סביב לדבק המגופה, שלא יצא ריח היין. ובימי שבט או ניסן, שמוכרין בעלי בתים חביות לחנווני כעשר או כט"ו יחד, נוטלין מגופותיהם וטועמין את היין, וחוזר וסותמו וטח בו טיט סביב המגופה, והוא קרוי רושם, ונושאן החנווני לביתו. ומתניתין בחבית רשומה, והיינו סימן, שיש רושמין, ויש שנושאין אותה פתוחה למוכרה מיד:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 23b:5:2.english: [Referring] to a marked [barrel] - Their barrels were made of earthenware, and they would seal them with an earthenware stopper and smear clay around [it] to adhere the stopper so that the aroma of the wine would not escape. And in the days of Shevat or Nisan, when householders sell barrels to a storekeeper, about ten or fifteen together, they remove their stoppers and taste the wine; and he closes it again and plasters clay upon it around the stopper — and that is called a mark [roshem] — and the storekeeper carries them to his home. And our Mishnah [speaks] of a marked barrel, and that is a distinguishing mark, for there are some who mark [them] and there are some who carry it open to sell it immediately.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 23b:5:3.hebrew: ופרכינן מכלל דברייתא - דקתני הרי אלו שלו, בפתוחה קתני, בתמיה? פשיטא, דהא אבידה מדעת היא, שהניחה פתוחה וכל שקצים ורמשים ונחשים שותים הימנה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 23b:5:3.english: And we ask: By inference, the baraita - which teaches "these belong to him" — does it teach about an open [barrel], [asked] in astonishment? It is obvious [that it belongs to the finder], for it is a deliberate loss, since he left it open and all [kinds of] creeping things, crawling creatures, and snakes drink from it.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 23b:5:4.hebrew: במציף - שהניח מגופה עליה ולא שרקה בטיט. סימן ליכא, ואבידה מדעת נמי ליכא:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 23b:5:4.english: With a floating [stopper] - That he placed a stopper upon it and did not seal it with clay. There is no distinguishing mark, and there is also no deliberate loss.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 23b:6:1.hebrew: קודם שנפתחו האוצרות - שעדיין לא הגיע זמן מוכרי החביות, ויחיד בעלמא הוא דעביד, הוי רושם סימן:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 23b:6:1.english: Before the storehouses were opened - Since the time of the barrel sellers had not yet arrived, and it was merely an individual who made [it], the seal is a distinguishing mark.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 23b:7:1.hebrew: ברקתא דנהרא - והיין בא לעיר בספינה, והלוקחין מפנין הספינה ומניחו על שפת הנהר, ונושאין אחת אחת, ופעמים ששוכח:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 23b:7:1.english: On the bank of the river - And the wine comes to the city by boat, and the buyers unload the boat and place it on the bank of the river, and they carry [the barrels] one by one, and sometimes [someone] forgets [one].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 23b:8:1.hebrew: איכא דאמרי כו' - נפקא מינה, דאפי' כוון ואמר מקום מושבה מסוים, לא הוי סימן:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 23b:8:1.english: Some say, etc. - The practical difference is that even if he pinpointed and stated a specific resting place [for it], it is not a distinguishing mark.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 23b:9:1.hebrew: כופרא - זפת, דבר שאין בו סימן הוה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 23b:9:1.english: Kufra - Pitch; it was something that has no distinguishing mark.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 23b:9:2.hebrew: מחסם - לשון לא תחסום (דברים כה), מגמגם בדבר ולבו נוקפו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 23b:9:2.english: Mechasem [hesitating] - An expression [related to] "You shall not muzzle [lo tachsom]" (Deuteronomy 25[:4]); [it means] he hesitates over the matter and his heart troubles him.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 23b:9:3.hebrew: דקדחו ביה חלפי - אורטי"א בלעז, גדלו עליה. ש"מ מימים רבים היה שם, וכבר נואשו הבעלים:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 23b:9:3.english: That chalfi sprouted through it - Ortie in Old French [nettles] grew upon it. From this we learn that it had been there for many days, and the owners had already despaired [of recovering it].

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 23b:11:1.hebrew: במסכת - וא"ת, והאמר (קדושין דף ל.) "ושננתם" — שיהו דברי תורה מחודדין בפיך, שאם ישאלך אדם אל תגמגם ותאמר לו, אלא אמור לו מיד? וי"ל, דהיינו דוקא באדם הבא לשאול דין או הוראה או להתלמד; אבל הכא, שבא לנסותו אם יודע, מותר לשנות ולומר "לא למדתי זה":
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 23b:11:1.english: With regard to a tractate - And if you should ask: Does it not state (Kiddushin 30a) [regarding the verse], "And you shall teach them diligently [veshinantam]," that the words of Torah should be sharp in your mouth, so that if a person asks you [something], do not stammer and tell him, rather tell him immediately? One can answer that this applies specifically to a person who comes to ask a law, a ruling, or to study; but here, where he comes to test him [to see] whether he knows [it], it is permitted to alter [the truth] and say, "I have not studied this."

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 23b:11:2.hebrew: בפוריא - אין רגילות שישאלוהו, כפירוש רש"י, אם שימש מטתו; אלא אם בעל קרי היה ולא בא לבית המדרש, ושאלוהו למה לא בא — ישנה ויאמר שחולה היה, או שאר אונס אירע לו. אי נמי: שאלוהו "שכבת על מטה זו?" — לא יאמר לו "כן", פן יראה בה קרי ויתגנה:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 23b:11:2.english: With regard to a bed - It is not customary for people to ask him, as Rashi explained, whether he had marital relations; rather, [it means that] if he had a seminal emission and did not come to the study hall, and they asked him why he did not come — he may alter [the truth] and say that he was ill, or that some other unavoidable circumstance befell him. Alternatively, [if] they asked him, "Did you sleep on this bed?" — he should not say to him, "Yes," lest a seminal emission be seen on it and he be disgraced.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 23b:1:1.hebrew: מחרוזות של דגים הרי אלו שלו - וה"ה מחרוזות של בשר, כדאמר בתוספתא (פ"ב). וא"ת: והא אמר בפ' גיד הנשה (חולין דף צה: ושם ד"ה בחרוזים): "אל תהא שוטה, בשר בחרוזים הוי סימן"? וי"ל: גבי בשר שנתעלם מן העין הקילו טפי. דאין הלכה כרב, מדפריך (שם): "ורב היכי אכל בשרא", משמע דאנן שפיר אכלינן:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 23b:1:1.english: "Strings of fish, these are his" - And the same applies to strings of meat, as it says in the Tosefta (Chapter 2). And if you will say: But did it not say in the chapter [entitled] Gid Hanasheh (Chullin 95b, and there s.v. Bacharuzim): "Do not be a fool, meat in strings is a distinguishing mark"? One can answer: Regarding meat that was out of sight, they were more lenient, for the halakha does not follow Rav, as [the Gemara] asks (there): "And how did Rav eat meat?", implying that we may properly eat [it].

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 23b:2:1.hebrew: מדמשקל הוי סימן מדה ומנין נמי הוי סימן - משמע דמדה עדיפא. וא"ת, והא אמרי' (לקמן בבא מציעא דף כח.): "ינתן לאומר משקלותיו ולא לאומר מדת ארכו ורחבו", משמע דמשקל הוי סימן טפי? וי"ל: דה"מ בבגד, דאין דרך לשקול — התם ודאי משקל עדיף:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 23b:2:1.english: "From [the fact] that weight is a distinguishing mark, measure and number are also a distinguishing mark" - This implies that measure is superior [to weight]. And if you say: But do we not say (later, Bava Metzia 28a): "It shall be given to the one who states its weight, and not to the one who states the measure of its length and its width," [which] implies that weight is a better distinguishing mark? One can answer that this applies to a garment, which is not usually weighed — there, weight is certainly superior.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 23b:3:1.hebrew: חביות של יין ושל גרוגרות הרי אלו שלו - אע"ג דתנן (לקמן בבא מציעא דף כד:) "מצא פירות בכלי חייב להכריז" משום סימן של הכלי, הכא רגילות הוא דכל החביות שוין. וא"ת: מדת היין להוי סימן? וי"ל, שהחבית מלאה וכל החביות שוין; אבל אם אין החבית מלאה, יהא סימן לומר כמה יין יש בו:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 23b:3:1.english: Barrels of wine and of dried figs, these belong to him - Even though we learned in a Mishnah (later, Bava Metzia 24b): "[If] one found produce in a vessel, he is obligated to proclaim [it]" because of the distinguishing mark of the vessel, here it is customary that all the barrels are alike. And if you ask: Let the measure of the wine serve as a distinguishing mark? One can answer that the barrel is full, and all the barrels are alike; however, if the barrel is not full, it would be a distinguishing mark to state how much wine is in it.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 23b:4:1.hebrew: אתלתא קרנתא - וא"ת, דרב אמר בפ' אין מעמידין (ע"ז דף לט: ושם): חבי"ת אסור בחותם אחד, ושמואל נמי לא פליג עליה אלא בחלב, אבל בשר, יין ותכלת מודה. ומפרש ר"ת דהתם מיירי בישראל חשוד, וכן משמע דמיירי התם לעיל בחבר ועם הארץ, וישראל חשוד לא מרתת כמו נכרי:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 23b:4:1.english: With three corners - And if you will ask: Rav said in the chapter [entitled] Ein Ma'amidin (Avodah Zarah 39b and there): Milk, meat, wine, and tekhelet are forbidden with [only] one seal, and Shmuel also disagrees with him only regarding milk, but regarding meat, wine, and tekhelet he agrees. And Rabbeinu Tam explains that there it is speaking of a suspect Jew, and so it is implied [from the fact] that it speaks there earlier of a chaver [scrupulous Jew] and an am ha'aretz [unlearned Jew], and a suspect Jew is not afraid [to tamper with a single seal] like a gentile.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 23b:5:1.hebrew: ברשום - שכל בעל הבית עושה רשימתו משונה משל חבירו, והוי סימן; ברייתא — בלא רשימה:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 23b:5:1.english: With a mark [i.e., sealed] - For every homeowner makes his mark different from that of his fellow, and it is a distinguishing mark; [whereas] the baraita [refers to a case] without a mark:

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 23b:6:1.hebrew: אביי אמר - אפילו רשום לא הוי סימן אחר שנפתחו האוצרות, שבעל הבית אחד מוכר להרבה חנוונים וכולם רשומים בענין אחד; ופרש"י אינו נראה:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 23b:6:1.english: Abaye said - Even a sealed [barrel] is not a distinguishing mark after the storehouses have been opened, for one homeowner sells to many storekeepers and they are all sealed in the same manner; and Rashi's explanation does not appear [correct].
